title: Screen a mannequin's arm with a detector wand: sweep over, then under it at 5 cm, slow at the watch until it alarms
instruction: Screen the mannequin's arm with the metal-detector wand: take the wand from its holder by its grip and sweep it over the top of the arm from shoulder to fingertips, then under the arm back to the shoulder, keeping the coil about 5 cm (two inches) off the arm and never touching it. Keep the wand moving, and slow down at the wristwatch until the wand's red lamp lights. Then lay the wand back flat in its holder, let go and move your hand clear.
context: Security guards (O*NET 33-9032.00; about 1.3 million US jobs, BLS 2024) have the Core task 'Operate detecting devices to screen individuals and prevent passage of prohibited articles into restricted areas.' Guards at venues, schools and courts screen with a hand wand. Garrett's SuperWand guide (1531500.B) says the wand detects metal only while it is in motion and is to be scanned within about two inches of the person. This task is one arm: the 48 cm wand is a lever held at its grip end, the arm tapers from 10 cm to 5.5 cm across, and the scan surface must follow it at that distance over the top and then under it without touching, the wand rolled round the arm between the passes. Too far or held still, the wand misses the watch; too close, it touches. O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA; task text used under CC BY 4.0. Garrett and Casio are named for identification only.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a 120 x 90 cm wood table, 75 cm high. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Mannequin arm: 70 cm from shoulder to fingertip; a round forearm 52 cm long, 10 cm across at the shoulder end tapering to 5.5 cm at the wrist, then a flat hand 18 cm long, 8 cm wide and 4 cm thick. It is held out sideways along y, palm down, its axis 32 cm above the table, its shoulder end at x 32, y -45 and its fingertips at y 25. Its stand: a bracket from the shoulder end to a 4 cm square mast at x 46, y -47, on a 14 cm square foot. A Casio MTP-1302D steel watch (case 44.2 x 38.5 x 9.2 mm, 105 g with band) sits on top of the wrist, its centre 6 cm short of the wrist end of the forearm (y 1). Wand: a Garrett SuperWand 1165800, 48.3 x 8.3 x 3.2 cm, 0.45 kg, with a 12 cm handle 3.2 cm square. The fingers take it 10 cm from the handle's end; its mass is spread through its shape, so its centre of mass is 17 cm beyond that point. The scan surface is the far 22 cm of the wand. It lies flat on its holder under the arm's shoulder end, its axis along y, its handle end at y -72 and its tip at y -24, the handle's centre line 12 cm above the table. The holder stands at x 32: two 3 cm square posts 10.3 cm tall, at y -68 under the handle, with a low stop either side of the handle, and at y -42 under the body. The red lamp near the handle lights while the wand moves at 2 cm/s or more with its scan surface within 5 cm of the watch case; it is dark when the wand is still or farther away. Both grippers start at the arms' ready pose. The left arm stays at rest; the score does not check which hand holds the wand. Start state, the same every trial: the wand at rest on the holder, the lamp dark.
scoring: Read from video of the wand's red lamp, with a foam gauge marked at 5 and 7 cm held to the arm for the stand-off, a tape for the holder and a photo for the wand lying flat. Score 0, and it stays 0, if the wand touches the arm, hand or watch at any time (in the simulation: any point of the wand within 2 mm, or any fingertip within 4 mm, of their surface). Otherwise cumulative, and nothing without the lamp: 0.25 once the lamp has lit (the scan surface within 5 cm of the watch case while the wand moves at 2 cm/s or more); 0.5 once a top pass is complete as well: every 5 cm stretch of the arm's 70 cm length has had the moving scan surface over it: the part over that stretch centred across the arm (its middle within the arm's half width of the arm's centre line), wholly higher than the arm's top there and within 7 cm of the arm; 0.75 once an underside pass is complete after that, the same but wholly lower than the arm's underside (a sweep along the arm's side counts for neither); 1.0 with the wand then back on the holder within 3 cm of its start place and 1 cm of its start height, lying flat (within 8 degrees), no fingertip within 3 cm of it and the wand still, held for 2 s; a wand that was let go more than 1.5 cm above the holder (dropped) does not reach 1.0.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the maker's sizes; the wand's mass is spread evenly through its shape; the fingers take the handle near the body. Lamp: lit by code when the scan surface is within 5 cm of the watch case and the wand moves at 2 cm/s or more. Garrett's manual says only 'scan within approximately two inches' and 'detects metal only while in motion'; it gives no watch range, and the 2 cm/s cut-off is ours. Touch is read from the wand's shapes and the fingertips. The switch is not modelled.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 on GPU physics: lamp lit at the watch, top and underside passes complete, no touch, wand back flat on its holder. Lazy routes: none 0, held still 0, 11 cm off 0, pressed in 0, top pass only 0.5, side sweep 0. Dream-1: 0.0 (one run).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials lay the wand flat on its holder and switch it on.
